prompt: In a roof truss, brace $\overrightarrow{BD}$ runs from the joint at $B$ into the interior of $\angle ABC$, splitting it into two smaller angles. If $\angle ABD = 32^\circ$ and $\angle DBC = 41^\circ$, what is $\angle ABC$ in degrees?
hint: The brace cuts the large angle into two smaller ones. How do the small pieces relate to the whole angle?

hints.text: The brace cuts the large angle into two smaller ones. How do the small pieces relate to the whole angle?
The Angle Addition Postulate says $\angle ABC = \angle ABD + \angle DBC$, so add $32$ and $41$.
$32 + 41 = 73$, so the whole angle $\angle ABC$ measures $73^\circ$.

explanation: Ray $\overrightarrow{BD}$ lies inside $\angle ABC$, so it divides that angle into two parts with no gap and no overlap.
The Angle Addition Postulate then says the parts add to the whole: $\angle ABC = \angle ABD + \angle DBC$.
Substituting the two measures gives $32 + 41 = 73$, so the whole angle is $\angle ABC = 73^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Same idea as segments
steps: Segment Addition stacks lengths; Angle Addition stacks turns.
Turn $32^\circ$, then turn $41^\circ$ more from the same joint — you have turned $73^\circ$ in all.
